what: Akien's RULED marker fires the ruling door in the same act he types it — /ruled <id> confirms a packet, bare /ruled lists open unmarked, /ruled <no-match> refuses loudly naming the store searched.
why: n=2 measured 2026-08-15: both confirmations of the authority ruling reached the door only because CC noticed 'so /ruled ...' in conversation and hand-ran confirm — the marker enforced by CC's attention, which is policy doing physics' job (Law 4). The skill makes his typing the command the confirmation, with no relay.
invoke: RETIRED — /ruled [<id>] (the slash face) and `cairn ruled [<id>]` (bin/cmd/ruled, a dispatcher into `python3 -m skills.ruled.door`) both exit 2 and print the replacement: `cairn question open --ticket <id> "<q?>" --why ...`, `cairn question answer <qid> "<his words>"`. Two faces, one door, one refusal.

Every mode exits 2 pointing at `cairn question open|answer|list`; decisions/ is read-only; the directory stays so the retirement is readable here. v0 first build 2026-08-27.

input_contract.id: optional — the ruling id to confirm. When present, the skill calls ruling.confirm(id, evidence) where evidence is the invocation itself. When absent, lists open unmarked rulings.
input_contract.evidence: derived from the invocation — his slash command IS his words verbatim.

how_it_learns: It does not — the skill is a thin pass-through to ruling.confirm/open_rulings/verify. The ruling machine's own learning (its proofs, its hook, its edges) covers the domain.
traces_to: Law 4 (the marker reaches the door because he typed it, not because CC was paying attention)
